A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PolarAPP. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original demosaicking, normal-estimation, de-reflection, ablation, and efficiency experiments, plus material-detection results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised PIDSR-based baseline results in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes the EIT loss from transforming low-resolution observations to transforming reconstructed images and resampling through A. However, v1's Fig. 4 already depicts the latter procedure. The PDFs therefore leave uncertain whether the implemented objective changed or its description was corrected. Architecture, feature alignment, and refinement remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use SfPUEL for normal estimation and material detection, PolarRGB for de-reflection, and Qiu plus real DoFP captures for demosaicking. Simulation and real-imaging scenarios are retained; the newly discussed sensor noise is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces the earlier PIDSR+SfPUEL and PIDSR+PolarFree combinations with PIDSR+ variants whose task networks are explicitly retrained on fixed PIDSR outputs. This revises the evaluated baseline variants, beyond renaming; the broader module combinations remain in Fig. 7.

E3.justification: Table 2 introduces task-network retraining on a frozen PIDSR demosaicker as a comparison control. Dataset splits, metrics, PolarAPP training budgets, and appendix evaluation settings remain unchanged. Newly specified EIT transformations are implementation disclosures, not established changes to prior settings.

E4.justification: Table 3, the alignment-weight sweep in Fig. 10, Grad-CAM analysis, and Appendix C's refinement and EIT ablations retain the same experiments and evidence. Revised explanations do not introduce additional ablation or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed information, repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix B retains the latency protocol of 100 inference runs, averaging the final 99.

E6.justification: Table 2 reports replacement baseline results under retraining: SfP 11.25-degree accuracy is 78.12%, versus 67.18% for the earlier combination; DfP LPIPS is 0.124 versus 0.178, now better than PolarAPP's unchanged 0.129. These are different baseline settings, not same-setting improvements. PolarAPP, ablation, efficiency, and material-detection scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 removes the sampling-commutation equation and reformulates EIT using reconstruction followed by transformation and resampling. Appendix A also corrects the task-loss target from the reference polarization image to task ground truth. The remaining bi-level gradient derivation is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty and performance claims: joint demosaicking and polarimetric tasks through meta-learned feature alignment, EIT, and task refinement.

C2.justification: Sections 1 and 4 replace distribution-mismatch explanations with the absence of task-aware feedback, including when task networks learn fixed demosaicker outputs. Section 4.3 narrows superiority to all SfP and main DfP metrics. Appendix F adds limitations concerning shared multi-task demosaicking and unmodeled shot/readout noise.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces code release 'upon acceptance' with a concrete repository link, whose contents were not accessed. Section 3.5 newly specifies a nonzero integer translation, 10-degree rotation, and horizontal flip. Real-imaging baseline preprocessing is clarified; existing hardware, training-time, and resolution details are retained.

R1.justification: The same 57 cited works, related-work sections, and principal novelty positioning are retained. Removing bibliography backreferences is a formatting change.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand EIT and task-comparison explanations, correct terminology, revise author information, and add acknowledgements. The section organization remains stable. The alignment-weight discussion introduces an incorrect reference to Fig. S2 instead of Fig. 10.

P2.justification: Fig. 6 rearranges existing comparison images with methods as rows. Algorithm 1 is reformatted, Table 2 labels and captions change, and a smaller page format and altered spacing reflow the document. The figure set and underlying qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: The retrained PIDSR controls strengthen the comparison beyond the earlier simple cascades. The revised EIT formulation better matches the existing diagram, while transformation details, a code link, and explicit noise and multi-task limitations improve documentation. These are bounded gains with unchanged coverage and PolarAPP scores; the incorrect alignment-weight figure reference is a small editorial drawback.
